latest.title: New Natural Hydrogen Contract Win
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 4780N
GETECH Group plc
23 July 2026
23 July 2026
Getech Group plc
("Getech" or the "Company")
Getech Wins Landmark €1m+ European Commission Natural Hydrogen Contract
European Commission Study to Quantify Subsurface Natural Hydrogen Reservoirs for Future Production in Europe
Getech, a leading locator of subsurface resources, has been selected as a key technical delivery partner in a consortium that has been awarded a major European Commission ("EC") contract to deliver the first Europe-wide assessment of natural hydrogen potential and associated regulatory requirements, with an expected contract value to Getech of more than €1 million, to be realised over the course of FY26 and FY27.
The 12-month study, commissioned by the Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs (DG GROW), is titled "Mapping underground reservoirs of natural hydrogen in Europe and developing the necessary legislation for sustainable production"
.
Getech will deliver the main geological components of the study as part of a consortium led by Trinomics B.V. ("Trinomics"). The project will
develop the first Europe-wide view
of the potential of Natural Hydrogen as a low carbon energy source by mapping geological settings favourable for natural hydrogen accumulations, across all EU Member States, assessing the feasibility of commercial extraction at selected locations and providing evidence-based recommendations to inform future regulation and market design.
The award follows a competitive EC procurement process assessing technical capability, sector expertise and the ability to deliver a consistent Europe-wide evaluation across all Member States
. In delivering the project, Getech will draw on its natural hydrogen exploration workflow experience, world-leading proprietary gravity and magnetic datasets and Globe geoscience platform, which together provide unique, consistent subsurface insight into this potentially transformative low carbon energy source. Getech's revenue for the project will comprise consultancy, data and software licence fees.
Chris Jepps, CEO at Getech, commented:
"
Being selected by the EC for this landmark natural hydrogen study is a strong validation of Getech's technical capabilities and investment
in natural hydrogen as an emerging resource. Natural hydrogen has the potential to play an important role in the EU's decarbonisation and energy security, and this project puts Getech at the centre of how the world evaluates natural hydrogen's potential and designs policy to support its responsible development.
For Getech, this contract is both financially material and gives the Company an unparalleled opportunity to further validate and refine its natural hydrogen exploration methodologies at continental scale
. The methodology and expertise we build through this study are directly transferable, and we see clear potential to scale this partnership model to other regions across the globe where natural hydrogen remains largely unexplored.
As hydrogen establishes itself as a pillar of the global energy transition, Getech's proprietary datasets and geoscientific insight will be of growing importance to governments, energy companies and regulators
worldwide."
Figure 1 - The growing global use of hydrogen by sector and the increasing demand for new hydrogen applications by 2030 (IEA 2026, licence: CC BY 4.0).
This project may also encourage other studies into this potentially transformational low carbon resource elsewhere in the world. Large parts of Africa, South America and Central Asia remain unexplored from a natural hydrogen perspective, despite strong geological indicators of substantial subsurface potential. Getech will be well positioned to participate in any such activities given its proprietary global datasets and the experience gained from this EC mandate providing a proven foundation from which to lead equivalent assessments.
​

About Getech
Getech provides trusted subsurface and geospatial insight to organisations across the global natural resources sector. We help corporates, governments, and regulators find and manage the subsurface resources essential to the evolving energy and minerals landscape by combining unique global earth‑science data, leading geospatial expertise and advanced analytics. Our solutions reduce risk, accelerate opportunities and enhance project value throughout the resource lifecycle, supporting activity across oil and gas, critical minerals, geothermal, natural hydrogen and other emerging resource domains.
Founded in 1994 Getech is listed on the Alternative Investment Market of the London Stock Exchange ("AIM"), with ticker symbol GTC.

company_30s.what_they_do: GTC Ltd. builds and supplies hydrogen‑generation equipment, mainly electrolyzers and fuel‑cell systems, aimed at commercial and industrial customers that need clean energy solutions.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Hydrogen is becoming a cornerstone of the low‑carbon transition, with governments worldwide offering incentives for clean‑energy infrastructure. GTC’s technology positions it to tap a rapidly expanding market that is still under‑served by established players.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in the early revenue phase, having recently secured a natural‑hydrogen contract. It is adjusting its capital structure through share‑option exercises and equity issuances, and has undergone a board change. The stock trades at a very low price, reflecting the steep discount investors have applied to the company’s prospects.

rns_narrative: GTC has just announced a win on a natural‑hydrogen contract, signalling a tangible revenue stream and validating its core technology.
The company has issued new equity and exercised share options, indicating a push to shore up cash reserves and potentially fund further expansion.
Recent governance moves—an AGM and a director change—suggest a fresh strategic direction and an effort to strengthen oversight.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Takeover chatter amid quiet market activity fuels a mix of cautious optimism.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Several community members highlight a potential buyer and speculate that a takeover could unlock value, citing the recent contract win as proof of the company’s viability.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others point out the lack of clear, consistent revenue and the risk of dilution from the equity issuance, warning that the stock could keep sliding if the takeover fails to materialise.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from indifferent to mildly bullish after the contract announcement, but the overall chatter remains low, suggesting most investors are still on the sidelines.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are dead, meaning a news event could trigger a surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: A formal takeover agreement or a clear commitment from a strategic buyer.
Completion of the new equity issuance and a positive cash‑flow statement from the hydrogen contract.
A significant uptick in trading volume that breaks the 50‑day moving average, signalling renewed interest.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals are a breakout above the 0.02p support level with volume exceeding 1.5× the 20‑day average, a clear announcement of buyer terms, or a sharp decline in the company’s debt profile.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a crash‑recovery cycle—capitulation has likely finished, but the mean‑reversion play is still in its formative phase. The APEX score suggests a moderate compression, so a decisive volume spike is needed to confirm the bounce.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The recent hydrogen contract win gives the company a real revenue source. If the price climbs to 0.20p (halfway to the 0.40p high seen in early 2025), the upside is roughly 200% from today’s price. With the APEX score above 8 and no obvious terminal risk, the asymmetry is heavily in favour of a breakout.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still relies on a single contract and has issued new equity, which could dilute existing shareholders. If the takeover talks break down or the contract fails to deliver, the price could fall back to 0.00p, wiping out any gains.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current price (essentially 0% if the stock stays flat). Potential gain could be 200% or more if the price reaches 0.20p. The risk‑reward ratio is therefore highly asymmetric in favour of the long side.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above 0.02p on volume > 1.5× the 20‑day average. Use a 20% stop‑loss below the entry level. Size the position for 10% of your discretionary trading capital to keep exposure manageable.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see either a clear takeover announcement or a volume spike that confirms the breakout. Watch for a 5‑day moving‑average cross above the 20‑day average as a secondary confirmation.
playbook.if_passing: If the company files for bankruptcy, delists, or the takeover collapses without any new contract, consider exiting to avoid further erosion of capital.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash followed by a new hydrogen contract win and takeover speculation creates a contrarian play with a high upside and limited downside—enter on a breakout above 0.02p and keep a tight stop.
